name: Notice of the State Council on Issuing the Overall Plan for the Beijing, Hunan, and Anhui Pilot Free Trade Zones and the Expansion Area Plan for the Zhejiang Pilot Free Trade Zone (excerpt) (Guo Fa [2020] No. 10) (State Council, August 30, 2020)
content: Further enrich the functions of the single window for international trade, and include the declaration of service trade export tax exemption in the management of the single window. Deepen the pilot innovation of service trade, promote the transformation and upgrading of service outsourcing to high technology, high quality, high efficiency, and high added value, accelerate the development of emerging service trades such as information services, cultural trade, and technology trade, and explore new formats and models of digital + service led by high-end services. Promote the construction of a traceability system for the quality of imported and exported products, and expand the types of traceable goods. Expand the scope of acceptance of third-party inspection results for goods and institutions.
titlelist: The main tasks and measures are to establish an institutional system with investment and trade liberalization and facilitation as the core, and further enhance the level of trade facilitation.

name: Notice of the State Council on Issuing the Overall Plan for the Beijing, Hunan, and Anhui Pilot Free Trade Zones and the Expansion Area Plan for the Zhejiang Pilot Free Trade Zone (excerpt) (Guo Fa [2020] No. 10) (State Council, August 30, 2020)
content: Focus on energy and food security. Research and establish a policy guarantee system that combines government reserves and enterprise reserves for major commodities such as energy, in order to better leverage the role of enterprise reserves in ensuring food security.
titlelist: Main tasks and measures, to construct a high-quality modern and open economic system, and to build a global resource allocation base for bulk commodities with oil and gas as the core.

name: Notice of the State Council on Issuing the Overall Plan for the Beijing, Hunan, and Anhui Pilot Free Trade Zones and the Expansion Area Plan for the Zhejiang Pilot Free Trade Zone (excerpt) (Guo Fa [2020] No. 10) (State Council, August 30, 2020)
content: Establish an international and domestic dual-loop supply policy system for key components. Take key core technologies as the breakthrough point, focus on industries such as new materials and life health, establish a responsibility system for the long-chain of the industrial chain, and enhance the ability to fill the chain. Explore the implementation of industrial chain land supply. Promote the high concentration of industrial clusters in space, close coordination between upstream and downstream, and intensive and efficient supply chain. Focus on advantageous industries such as high-performance magnetic materials, new membrane materials, and advanced carbon materials, and proactively layout emerging fields such as intelligent composite materials and marine new materials, accelerate the key core technology research and development and achievement transformation of the upgrading of the new materials industry, actively promote the construction of advanced materials industry innovation centers, and create an important platform for participating in global new materials industry innovation competition. Focus on the application of new generation intelligent technologies, vigorously introduce several top domestic and foreign intelligent manufacturing demonstration enterprises, support local enterprises in promoting international collaborative research and development, actively integrate into the global supply chain, innovation chain, and value chain of high-end manufacturing industry. Build a domestic important base for intelligent manufacturing equipment industry around modern high-end CNC machine tools, robots, and other intelligent equipment and key basic components. Implement tax policies to support the import of scientific and technological innovation, and exempt import taxes on scientific research equipment imported by units in the area that meet the policy requirements.
titlelist: The main tasks and measures are to build a high-quality modern and open economic system and create an advanced manufacturing cluster.

name: Opinions of the State Council on Supporting Shanxi Province in Further Deepening Reform and Promoting the Transformation and Development of Resource-based Economy (excerpt) (State Council [2017] No. 42) (State Council/September 1, 2017)
content: Guide the exit of excess capacity, develop high-quality capacity, promote the reduction and replacement of coal capacity, and promote the reduction and reorganization. Fully implement ultra-low emission and energy-saving transformation of coal-fired units, appropriately control the scale of thermal power, and implement intelligent transformation of energy production and utilization facilities. Optimize the energy industry structure, focus on the layout of high-end projects such as coal deep processing and coalbed methane conversion, and new energy power generation bases. Study the layout of coal storage and distribution bases. Encourage the comprehensive utilization of coal mine resources such as coal gangue, mine water, and coal mine gas. According to changes in the electricity market demand, study the feasibility of planning and constructing new outbound channels in a timely manner to improve the outbound capacity of power transmission in Shanxi. Layout mobile energy industries such as solar thin films and create a leader in mobile energy. Actively implement multi-energy complementary integrated optimization demonstration projects in newly built industrial parks and existing industrial parks with conditions, and promote the comprehensive utilization of energy in a hierarchical manner. Build overseas demonstration bases for coal mining and clean and efficient utilization of coal as the main body of enterprises.
titlelist: Strengthen the mechanism for promoting industrial transformation and upgrading, build a pioneer in energy revolution, and promote the revolution in energy supply.

name: Opinions of the State Council on Supporting Shanxi Province in Further Deepening Reform and Promoting the Transformation and Development of Resource-based Economy (excerpt) (State Council [2017] No. 42) (State Council/September 1, 2017)
content: The country gives special emphasis to Shanxi Province in the layout of major productive forces, especially in the strategic emerging industries. It supports the construction of innovation and entrepreneurship capabilities in old industrial cities in Shanxi Province, and accelerates the transformation of old and new driving forces. It supports the establishment of intelligent manufacturing innovation centers and innovation centers for new materials such as aluminum-magnesium alloys and carbon fibers in Shanxi Province. It supports Shanxi Province in actively connecting with eastern provinces and cities such as Beijing, Tianjin, and Hebei, exploring the establishment of cooperation mechanisms, conducting exchanges and targeted training of officials, and learning from the advanced experiences and practices of nurturing and developing emerging industries in the eastern region.
titlelist: Strengthen the mechanism for promoting industrial transformation and upgrading, create a leading force in the energy revolution, and establish a mechanism for nurturing and supporting emerging industries.

name: Guiding Opinions of the State Council on Promoting Enterprise Technological Transformation (excerpt) (State Council [2012] No. 44) (State Council/September 1, 2012)
content: In order to address key areas and weak links, breakthroughs will be made in a batch of common key technologies, accelerating the industrial application of advanced technologies. This will improve the domestic guarantee capability of basic raw materials and components, major equipment, and core technologies. It will also enhance the level of research and formulation of technical standards, and promote the improvement of technological innovation capabilities. Encouragement and support will be given to the transformation and upgrading of innovative carriers such as enterprise technology centers, engineering laboratories, and major scientific and technological infrastructure. A group of technology innovation demonstration enterprises with a solid research and development foundation, multiple intellectual property rights, and strong industry driving force will be cultivated. Open cooperation will be strengthened to enhance enterprise innovation capabilities. Efforts will be made to establish a collaborative innovation system with enterprises as the main body, integrating industry, academia, research, and application. Active exploration will be conducted to lead industrial development with technical standards and to promote entrepreneurship based on innovative achievements. This will facilitate the close integration of scientific research and production, fully leveraging the creativity and enthusiasm of market entities, and accelerating the industrialization of scientific and technological achievements.
titlelist: Key tasks: Promote technological innovation and industrialization of scientific and technological achievements.

name: Guiding Opinions of the State Council on Promoting Enterprise Technological Transformation (excerpt) (State Council [2012] No. 44) (State Council/September 1, 2012)
content: Accelerate the elimination of outdated technology and equipment, promote the application of advanced manufacturing systems such as automation, digitization, networking, and intelligence, as well as intelligent manufacturing equipment and large-scale technical equipment. Support key enterprises in targeting cutting-edge technologies, accelerate equipment upgrading and transformation, and promote the attainment of international advanced levels in key areas of technological equipment. Implement equipment innovation projects to continuously improve the technological level of the equipment manufacturing industry.
titlelist: Key task, improve equipment level.

content: Adhere to the path of China's new type of industrialization with Chinese characteristics, adapt to changes in market demand, follow the new trend of technological progress, leverage the comparative advantages of our country's industries in the global economy, and develop a modern industrial system that is optimized in structure, technologically advanced, clean and safe, with high added value, and strong employment absorption capacity.

name: Outline of the Twelfth Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development of the People's Republic of China (excerpt) (State Council/16th March 2011)
content: Vigorously develop strategic emerging industries such as energy conservation and environmental protection, new generation information technology, biotechnology, high-end equipment manufacturing, new energy, new materials, and new energy vehicles. The energy conservation and environmental protection industry focuses on the development of key technologies, equipment, products, and services for efficient energy conservation, advanced environmental protection, and resource recycling. The new generation information technology industry focuses on the development of new generation mobile communications, next-generation internet, convergence of three networks, Internet of Things, cloud computing, integrated circuits, new display technologies, high-end software, high-end servers, and information services. The biotechnology industry focuses on the development of biomedicine, biomedical engineering products, biotechnology in agriculture, and biomanufacturing. The high-end equipment manufacturing industry focuses on the development of aviation equipment, satellites and applications, rail transportation equipment, and intelligent manufacturing equipment. The new energy industry focuses on the development of new generation nuclear energy, solar thermal utilization and photovoltaic power generation, wind power technology and equipment, smart grids, and biomass energy. The new materials industry focuses on the development of new functional materials, advanced structural materials, high-performance fibers and their composites, and common basic materials. The new energy vehicle industry focuses on the development of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, pure electric vehicles, and fuel cell vehicles. The added value of strategic emerging industries accounts for about 8% of the country's total GDP.
titlelist: Transformation and upgrading to enhance the core competitiveness of industries, cultivating and developing strategic emerging industries, and promoting leapfrog development in key areas.

name: 14th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the Robot Industry (excerpt) (MIIT Joint Regulation [2021] No. 206) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Science and Technology, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, National Health Commission, Ministry of Emergency Management, People's Bank of China, State Administration for Market Regulation, China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, China Securities Regulatory Commission, State Administration of Defense Science, Technology and Industry for National Defense, State Administration of Work Safety/December 28, 2021)
content: By 2025, China will become a global source of innovation in robot technology, a hub for high-end manufacturing, and a new frontier for integrated applications. Breakthroughs will be made in core robot technologies and high-end products, with overall performance reaching international advanced levels and key component performance and reliability reaching the same level as similar international products. The annual growth rate of the robot industry's revenue will exceed 20%. A number of internationally competitive leading enterprises and a large number of innovative and high-growth small giant enterprises with strong capabilities will be formed, and 3-5 industry clusters with international influence will be established. name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: Intelligent manufacturing is based on the deep integration of advanced manufacturing technology and new generation information technology. It spans the entire product lifecycle, including design, production, management, and service. It features self-perception, self-decision-making, self-execution, self-adaptation, and self-learning. Its goal is to improve the quality, efficiency, and flexibility of advanced production methods in the manufacturing industry. The architecture of intelligent manufacturing systems describes the elements, equipment, activities, and other contents involved in intelligent manufacturing from three dimensions: lifecycle, system hierarchy, and intelligent features. It is mainly used to clarify the standardized objects and scope of intelligent manufacturing.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: The lifecycle covers various stages from product prototype development to product recycling and remanufacturing, including a series of interconnected value creation activities such as design, production, logistics, sales, and services. The activities in the lifecycle can be iteratively optimized and have characteristics of sustainable development. The composition and chronological order of the lifecycle vary in different industries. (1) Design refers to the process of implementing and optimizing requirements based on all constraints of the enterprise and the selected technology. (2) Production refers to the process of creating products through activities such as material processing, transportation, assembly, and inspection. (3) Logistics refers to the physical flow process of goods from the supply location to the receiving location. (4) Sales refers to the business activities of transferring products or goods from the enterprise to customers. (5) Services refer to the process and results of a series of activities generated during the interaction between product providers and customers.
titlelist: Intelligent manufacturing system architecture, lifecycle

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: The system hierarchy refers to the hierarchical division of organizational structure related to enterprise production activities, including the equipment layer, unit layer, workshop layer, enterprise layer, and collaborative layer. (1) The equipment layer refers to the hierarchical level where the enterprise utilizes sensors, instruments, machinery, devices, etc., to realize actual physical processes and perceive and control physical processes. (2) The unit layer refers to the hierarchical level used for processing information within the enterprise and realizing monitoring and control of physical processes. (3) The workshop layer is the hierarchical level that implements production management for factories or workshops. (4) The enterprise layer is the hierarchical level that implements business management for the enterprise. (5) The collaborative layer is the hierarchical level where the enterprise achieves internal and external information interconnection and sharing, and realizes cross-enterprise business collaboration.
titlelist: Intelligent manufacturing system architecture, system hierarchy.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: Intelligent features refer to the characteristics of manufacturing activities that have functions such as self-perception, self-decision-making, self-execution, self-learning, and self-adaptation. This includes five levels of intelligent requirements: resource elements, interconnection, fusion sharing, system integration, and emerging formats. (1) Resource elements refer to the level where the resources or tools needed by the enterprise for production and their digital models are located. (2) Interconnection refers to the level where data transmission and parameter semantic exchange between resource elements are achieved through wired or wireless networks, communication protocols, and interfaces. (3) Fusion sharing refers to the level where information collaboration and sharing are achieved based on interconnection, utilizing new generation information and communication technologies such as cloud computing and big data. (4) System integration refers to the level where data exchange and functional interconnection between equipment, production units, production lines, digital workshops, intelligent factories, and intelligent manufacturing systems are realized during the intelligent manufacturing process. (5) Emerging formats refer to the level where data, models, and systems integrating and merging different levels of resource elements in physical space and digital space are established. These formats cover functions such as cognition, diagnosis, prediction, and decision-making, and support virtual and real iterative optimization.
titlelist: Intelligent manufacturing system architecture, intelligent features.

The development of intelligent equipment standards such as human-machine collaboration systems, process equipment, and inspection and testing equipment will be accelerated. Intelligent factory standards such as intelligent factory design and integrated optimization, smart supply chain standards such as supply chain collaboration and evaluation, intelligent service standards such as network collaborative manufacturing, and intelligent technology standards such as digital twins and artificial intelligence applications will be established. Industrial network standards such as industrial network integration will support the development of intelligent manufacturing to a new level. By 2025, a relatively complete cluster of standards will be formed in areas such as digital twins, data dictionaries, human-machine collaboration, smart supply chains, system reliability, network security, and functional safety. Gradually, an intelligent manufacturing standard system that adapts to technological innovation trends, meets industry development needs, and benchmarks international advanced levels will be constructed.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: The architecture of the intelligent manufacturing standard system includes three parts: A Basic Commonality, B Key Technologies, and C Industry Applications, which mainly reflect the composition relationship of each part of the standard system. Specifically, the A Basic Commonality standards include six categories: general, safety, reliability, testing, evaluation, and personnel capability. They are located at the bottom layer of the intelligent manufacturing standard system architecture and provide support for the B Key Technologies standards and C Industry Applications standards. The B Key Technologies standards are the projection of the intelligent characteristics dimension of the intelligent manufacturing system architecture in terms of the lifecycle dimension and system level dimension. Among them, the BA Intelligent Equipment standards mainly focus on the resource elements of the intelligent characteristics dimension, the BB Intelligent Factory standards mainly focus on the resource elements and system integration of the intelligent characteristics dimension, the BC Smart Supply Chain corresponds to the interconnection, integration, and system integration of the intelligent characteristics dimension, the BD Intelligent Services correspond to the emerging formats of the intelligent characteristics dimension, the BE Intelligent Empowerment Technologies correspond to the resource elements, interconnection, integration, system integration, and emerging formats of the intelligent characteristics dimension, and the BF Industrial Networks correspond to the interconnection and system integration of the intelligent characteristics dimension. The C Industry Applications standards are located at the top layer of the intelligent manufacturing standard system architecture, targeting specific industry needs, and refining and implementing the A Basic Commonality standards and B Key Technologies standards, guiding various industries in promoting intelligent manufacturing.
titlelist: Construction ideas, intelligent manufacturing standard system architecture

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: It mainly includes four parts: terminology definition, reference model, metadata and data dictionary, and identification. The definition standards are used to unify the concepts related to intelligent manufacturing and provide support for the development of other standards, including terminology, vocabulary, symbols, codes, and other standards. The reference model standards are used to help all parties understand and comprehend the objects, boundaries, hierarchical relationships, and inherent connections of standardization in intelligent manufacturing, including reference models, system architectures, and other standards. The metadata and data dictionary standards are used to specify the classification, naming rules, description and expression, registration and management maintenance requirements, as well as the establishment methods of industrial data involved in intelligent manufacturing product design, production, circulation, and other processes, including metadata, data dictionary, and other standards. The identification standards are used for the identification and resolution of various objects in the field of intelligent manufacturing, including identification codes, code transmission rules, object metadata, resolution systems, and other standards.

content: It mainly includes two parts: functional safety and network security. Functional safety standards are used to ensure that control systems can correctly and reliably perform their safety functions when hazards occur, thereby avoiding production accidents caused by system failures or conflicts with safety facilities. This includes safety collaboration requirements for intelligent manufacturing, functional safety system design and implementation, functional safety testing and evaluation, functional safety management, and functional safety operation and maintenance standards. Network security standards are used to ensure the availability, confidentiality, and integrity of information systems related to intelligent manufacturing, thereby ensuring the safe and reliable operation of the systems. This includes security standards for connected devices, control systems, networks (including identity resolution systems), industrial internet platform security, data security, as well as related security product evaluations, system security design, security maturity assessment, and encryption applications.
titlelist: Construction content, basic common standards, safety standards.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT-Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)

The engineering management standards mainly plan, organize, coordinate, and supervise the reliability activities of intelligent manufacturing systems, including reliability requirements, reliability management, integrated support management, and life cycle cost management of intelligent manufacturing systems and their hierarchical objects. The technical methods standards are mainly used to guide the specific reliability assurance and verification work of intelligent manufacturing systems and their hierarchical levels, including reliability design, reliability prediction, reliability testing, reliability analysis, reliability growth, and reliability evaluation.

content: It mainly includes three parts: testing requirements, testing methods, and testing techniques. The testing requirements standards are used to guide the scientific arrangement and effective management of intelligent equipment and systems during the testing process, including consistency and interoperability of different types of intelligent equipment and systems, integration and interconnection, system efficiency, electromagnetic compatibility, and other testing items, indicators, or requirements. The testing methods standards are used for testing different types of intelligent equipment and systems, including standards for test content, methods, steps, processes, calculations, analysis, as well as standards for performance, environmental adaptability, and parameter calibration. The testing techniques standards are used to standardize the detection techniques for intelligent manufacturing, including standards for judgmental testing, informative testing, causal testing, etc. The detection methods are not limited to software and hardware testing, online monitoring, simulation testing, etc.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: The main parts include sensors and instruments, automatic identification equipment, human-machine collaboration systems, control systems, additive manufacturing equipment, industrial robots, CNC machine tools, process equipment, inspection and testing equipment, and others. It mainly specifies the information model, data dictionary, communication protocols and interfaces, integration and interoperability, operation and maintenance services, performance evaluation, testing methods, and other requirements for intelligent equipment. (1) Standards for sensors and instruments. It mainly includes general technical standards such as characteristics and classification, reliability design, life prediction, system and component lifecycle management, and performance evaluation; interfaces and communication standards such as information models, data interfaces, field device integration, semantic interoperability, communication protocols, and protocol consistency.(2) Standards for automatic identification equipment. It mainly includes general technical standards such as data encoding, performance evaluation, and equipment management; interfaces and communication standards such as interface specifications, communication protocols, information integration, fusion perception, and collaborative information processing.(3) Standards for human-machine collaboration systems. It mainly includes professional graphic symbol classification and definition of virtual reality/augmented reality (VR/AR), industrial intelligent interaction terminals, visual image acquisition and recognition, virtual and real fusion information display, and textual and graphic image standards; as well as interaction and collaboration standards such as cooperation mode requirements, task allocation requirements, and human-machine interfaces in the process of human-machine collaboration.(4) Standards for control systems. It mainly includes general technical standards such as control methods, data acquisition and storage, human-machine interface and visualization, and testing; interfaces and communication standards such as control device information models, clock synchronization, interfaces, system interconnection, and protocol consistency; programming standards such as engineering data exchange, control logic programs, control program architecture, control tags and data flow, and function blocks.(5) Standards for additive manufacturing equipment. It mainly includes general technical standards such as model data quality and processing requirements, establishment and classification of process knowledge bases, data dictionaries, and coding requirements; interfaces and communication standards such as system and equipment information models, communication protocols; testing and evaluation standards such as testing methods and performance evaluation.(6) Standards for industrial robots. It mainly includes general technical standards such as data formats, object dictionaries; interfaces and communication standards between information models, programming systems, users, and industrial robots; collaborative standards between industrial robots and humans, environments, systems, and other equipment; testing and evaluation standards such as performance and adaptability to environments.(7) Standards for CNC machine tools. It mainly includes general technical standards such as machine tool and functional component languages and formats, fault information dictionaries, classifications, and control requirements; interfaces and collaboration standards such as programming interfaces, physical mapping models, interconnection, and interoperability; testing and monitoring standards such as detection, status monitoring, and optimization based on industrial cloud manufacturing.(8) Standards for process equipment. It mainly includes general technical standards such as process equipment technology requirements for casting, forging, welding, heat treatment, and special processing applied to process and discrete manufacturing; interfaces and monitoring standards such as data interfaces and status monitoring.(9) Standards for inspection and testing equipment. It mainly includes general technical standards such as online inspection system data formats, performance and environmental requirements; integration standards such as interconnection and interfaces between inspection and testing equipment and other production equipment and systems; equipment management standards such as performance status detection and calibration, fault diagnosis.(10) Other standards. It mainly includes general technical standards such as data encoding, data formats, performance and environmental requirements for intelligent equipment used in warehousing, logistics, printing, etc.; interfaces and communication standards such as information models, interoperability, interface specifications, communication protocols, and protocol consistency. The key focus of intelligent equipment standardization includes standards for sensors and instruments such as reliability design and performance evaluation; interfaces and communication standards such as information models, data interfaces, and protocol consistency. Standards for automatic identification equipment such as data encoding and performance evaluation; interfaces and communication standards such as interface specifications and fusion perception and collaborative information processing. Standards for human-machine collaboration systems such as visual image acquisition and recognition; interaction and collaboration standards such as cooperation mode requirements, task allocation requirements, and human-machine interfaces. Standards for control systems such as control device information models, system interconnection, and protocol consistency; programming standards such as engineering data exchange, control tags and data flow, and function blocks. Standards for additive manufacturing equipment such as model data quality and processing requirements, data dictionaries, and communication protocols. Standards for industrial robots such as data formats and object dictionaries; interfaces and communication standards between programming systems, users, and industrial robots; collaborative standards between industrial robots and humans, environments, systems, and other equipment. Standards for CNC machine tools such as machine tool and functional component languages and formats, fault information dictionaries; interfaces and collaboration standards such as programming interfaces, physical mapping models, and interconnection; testing and monitoring standards such as status monitoring and optimization. Standards for process equipment such as process equipment technology requirements, data interfaces, and status monitoring. Standards for inspection and testing equipment such as online inspection system data formats, performance and environmental requirements; integration standards such as interconnection and interfaces; equipment management standards such as performance status detection and calibration, fault diagnosis. Other standards such as data encoding, data formats, performance and environmental requirements; interfaces and communication standards such as information models, interoperability, interface specifications, communication protocols, and protocol consistency.
titlelist: Construction content, key technical standards, intelligent equipment standards.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: The main provisions include the process of intelligent factory design and delivery, as well as the content of factory design, production, management, logistics, and system integration. (1) Intelligent factory design standards. This mainly includes overall planning standards such as design requirements, design models, design verification, design document depth requirements, and collaborative design for intelligent factories; physical factory data collection, factory layout, virtual factory reference architecture, process flow and layout models, production process models and organizational models, simulation analysis, and information exchange between physical and virtual factories, etc. Physical/virtual factory design standards. (2) Intelligent factory delivery standards. This mainly includes digital delivery standards and intelligent factory project completion acceptance requirements, such as general requirements, content requirements, and quality requirements during the design and implementation stages. (3) Intelligent design standards. This mainly includes product design and simulation standards based on data-driven parametric modular design, model-based systems engineering (MBSE) design, collaborative design and simulation, multi-disciplinary coupled simulation optimization, and digital design of formula products; process design and simulation standards based on digital models of manufacturing resources; experimental design and simulation standards such as test methods, test data, and process management. (4) Intelligent production standards. This mainly includes planning and scheduling standards such as planning modeling and simulation, multi-level planning coordination, visual scheduling, and dynamic optimization; production execution standards such as automatic issuance and execution of operation files, design and manufacturing collaboration, dynamic organization of manufacturing resources, process simulation, production process control and optimization, exception management, and error prevention mechanisms; quality control standards such as intelligent online quality monitoring, early warning and optimization control, quality records, and quality traceability; equipment operation and maintenance standards based on knowledge, maintenance, fault management, etc. (5) Intelligent management standards. This mainly includes procurement management standards such as quality inspection and analysis of raw materials and auxiliary materials; sales management standards such as sales forecasting and customer service management; asset management standards such as equipment health and reliability management, knowledge management; energy management standards such as energy flow management and energy efficiency evaluation; safety management standards such as process control, emergency management, hazardous chemical management; environmental management standards such as real-time monitoring, forecasting and early warning. (6) Intelligent factory logistics standards. This mainly includes intelligent warehousing standards such as material status identification and information tracking within the factory, job assignment and scheduling optimization, and warehouse system functional requirements; intelligent distribution standards such as material sorting, distribution path planning and management. (7) Integrated optimization standards. This mainly includes integration standards such as software and hardware integration and system solution integration services that meet the business activity requirements within the factory; optimization standards such as operation and control optimization, data-driven full lifecycle business optimization. Key points of intelligent factory standard construction. Intelligent factory design standards. Overall planning standards such as intelligent factory functional requirements, collaborative design requirements; standards for information exchange between physical and virtual factories. Intelligent factory delivery standards. General requirements, content requirements, quality requirements, and delivery standards for digital delivery during the design and implementation stages, as well as intelligent factory project completion acceptance standards. Intelligent design standards. Product design and simulation standards based on data-driven parametric modular design, MBSE design, collaborative design and simulation, etc.; process design and simulation standards based on digital models of manufacturing resources. Intelligent production standards. Planning and scheduling standards such as planning modeling and simulation, multi-level planning coordination, etc.; production execution standards such as design and manufacturing collaboration, dynamic organization of manufacturing resources, production process control and optimization, etc.; quality control standards such as intelligent online quality monitoring and early warning, quality records and quality traceability; equipment management standards based on knowledge such as equipment status monitoring and optimization, maintenance, fault management. Integrated optimization standards. Integration standards such as software and hardware integration, system solution integration services that meet the business activity requirements within the factory; optimization standards such as operation and control optimization, data-driven full lifecycle business optimization.
titlelist: The content of construction, key technical standards, and intelligent factory standards mainly include seven parts: intelligent factory design, intelligent factory delivery, intelligent design, intelligent production, intelligent management, factory intelligent logistics, and integrated optimization.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: It mainly includes three parts: supply chain construction, supply chain management, and supply chain evaluation. It mainly specifies the technical and management requirements for data, processes, and evaluation in the cooperation process of upstream and downstream enterprises in the supply chain, guiding the design and development of supply chain management systems and platforms to ensure horizontal integration and efficient collaboration in the supply chain. The supply chain construction standards mainly include standards for data sharing, system construction and deployment, and integration and optimization of internal and external resources of upstream and downstream in the supply chain. The supply chain management standards mainly include supplier classification and performance evaluation standards, as well as standards for collaborative management of design, production, logistics, sales, and service in the supply chain. The supply chain evaluation standards mainly include risk identification and evaluation, risk warning and prevention control, performance indicator system, testing and evaluation methods, and other performance evaluation standards. The focus is on the construction of smart supply chain standards. Supply chain construction standards include standards for data formats, system construction and deployment, resource integration and optimization of upstream and downstream in the supply chain. Supply chain management standards include supplier classification and performance evaluation, as well as standards for collaborative design, production, logistics, sales, and service in the supply chain. Supply chain evaluation standards include risk identification and evaluation, risk warning and prevention control, performance indicator system, testing and evaluation methods, and other standards.
titlelist: Construction content, key technical standards, smart supply chain standards.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: It mainly includes three parts: large-scale personalized customization, operation and maintenance services, and network collaborative manufacturing. It is mainly used to achieve the integration of products and services, the organic integration of decentralized manufacturing resources, and the highly coordinated core competencies of each other, solving the problem of comprehensive utilization of various internal and external resources of the enterprise and providing various standardized and reliable new services. The standards for large-scale personalized customization mainly include general requirements, demand interaction requirements, design requirements, production requirements, evaluation and diagnosis, etc. The standards for operation and maintenance services mainly include general requirements, knowledge base, status monitoring, fault diagnosis, life prediction, operation and maintenance execution, etc. The standards for network collaborative manufacturing mainly include overall architecture, platform technology requirements, collaborative interaction processes, resource models and optimization configuration, implementation guidelines, etc. The focus is on the construction of intelligent services. Standards for operation and maintenance services include knowledge base, status monitoring, fault diagnosis, life prediction, operation and maintenance execution, etc. Standards for network collaborative manufacturing include overall architecture, platform technology requirements, collaborative interaction processes, resource models and optimization configuration, implementation guidelines, etc.
titlelist: Construction content, key technical standards, intelligent service standards.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: It mainly includes seven parts: artificial intelligence, industrial big data, industrial software, industrial cloud, edge computing, digital twin, and blockchain. It is mainly used to guide the integration and application of new technologies in the manufacturing industry and improve the level of manufacturing intelligence. (1) Artificial intelligence standards. It mainly includes knowledge service standards such as machine learning, knowledge representation, knowledge modeling, knowledge fusion, and knowledge computation; platform and support standards such as application platform architecture and integration requirements; performance evaluation standards such as training data requirements, testing guidelines, and evaluation principles; application management standards for product lifecycle such as intelligent online detection and operation management optimization.(2) Industrial big data standards. It mainly includes industrial big data platform standards such as platform construction requirements, operation and maintenance, and detection evaluation; data processing standards such as industrial big data collection, preprocessing, analysis, visualization, and access; data management and governance standards such as data management system, data resource management, data quality management, master data management, and data management capability maturity; data circulation standards such as internal data sharing in factories and external data exchange.(3) Industrial software standards. It mainly includes software product and system standards such as functional definition, business model, quality requirements, and maturity requirements for products, tools, embedded software, systems, and platforms; software system integration and interface standards such as industrial software interface specifications, integration rules, and product line engineering; service and management standards such as lifecycle management, quality management, asset management, configuration management, reliability requirements, and testing and verification; industrial technology software standards such as industrial technology software reference architecture and industrial application software packaging.(4) Industrial cloud standards. It mainly includes resource standards such as platform construction and application, access, configuration, and management of industrial cloud resources and service capabilities; service standards such as implementation guidelines, capability assessment, and effectiveness evaluation.(5) Edge computing standards. It mainly includes standards such as architecture and technical requirements, interfaces, edge network requirements, data management requirements, and edge operating systems.(6) Digital twin standards. It mainly includes general requirements standards such as reference architecture and information model; functional requirements standards for different system levels; data interaction and interface standards for integration and collaboration between digital twin systems; testing and evaluation standards such as performance evaluation and compliance testing; digital twin service application standards for different manufacturing scenarios.(7) Blockchain standards. It mainly includes process management standards such as industrial product development and traceability, service and quality management based on blockchain technology; and business process standards such as supply chain finance, cross-border trade and electronic contracts, procurement, and logistics based on blockchain for manufacturing enterprises. The key focus of intelligent empowerment technology standards construction includes artificial intelligence standards such as knowledge service standards, performance evaluation standards, and platform and support standards for knowledge services, performance evaluation standards, and platform and support standards for intelligent online detection and operation management optimization in product lifecycle scenarios; edge computing standards such as architecture and technical requirements, interface standards, edge network requirements, data management requirements, and edge operating systems; digital twin standards such as general requirements, reference architecture, data interaction and interface, service applications; and blockchain standards such as industrial product traceability, industrial design copyright protection, trusted quality management, supply chain finance, and electronic contracts based on blockchain.
titlelist: Construction content, key technical standards, intelligent empowerment technology standards.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: It mainly includes four parts: industrial wireless networks, industrial wired networks, industrial network integration, and industrial network resource management. It is mainly used to meet the low latency, high reliability, and other requirements within and between different system levels in factories, to achieve networking between different levels and heterogeneous networks under industrial network architecture, and to standardize the technical requirements for network addressing, service quality, radio frequency, and network operation management. Industrial wireless network standards mainly include wireless local area networks (WLAN), wireless addressable remote sensor high-speed channels (WirelessHART), industrial wireless networks for factory automation/process automation (WIA-FA/PA), narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT), 5G applications, and other standards. Industrial wired network standards mainly include fieldbuses, industrial Ethernet, industrial passive optical network (PON), industrial structured cabling, and other standards. Industrial network integration standards mainly include deterministic networking (DetNet), information technology/operational technology (IT/OT) integration, interconnection between heterogeneous networks, and other standards. Industrial network resource management standards mainly include network management, network address management, network spectrum management, software-defined networking (SDN), and other standards. The focus of industrial network standard construction includes industrial wireless network standards, 5G application standards, industrial network integration standards, IT/OT integration, interconnection between heterogeneous networks, and industrial network resource management standards, such as network management, network address management, network spectrum management, SDN, and other standards.
titlelist: Construction content, key technical standards, industrial network standards.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT-Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: It mainly includes 12 parts: ship and marine engineering equipment, building materials, petrochemicals, textiles, steel, rail transportation, aerospace, automobiles, non-ferrous metals, electronic information, power equipment, and others. It leverages the guiding and supporting role of basic common standards and key technical standards in the formulation of industry standards, emphasizes the coordination and support between industry standards and national standards, combines industry characteristics, focuses on the development of normative, regulatory, and guideline-type application standards, and further promotes or improves the industry's intelligent manufacturing standard system. It also analyzes the key directions of intelligent manufacturing standardization in light industry, food industry, agricultural machinery, engineering machinery, nuclear energy, and civil explosives.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT-Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the characteristics of multi-variety, small-batch, and customization in the manufacturing of ships and marine engineering equipment, considering the application needs of digital new infrastructure such as 5G, standards and specifications such as coding, data dictionary, and 5G application technology requirements are formulated for ship assembly and construction. Standards or regulations are also established for information system interfaces, overall planning of production lines, and collaborative product design around the construction of intelligent shipyards.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, ship and marine engineering equipment.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the characteristics of multiple subdivisions and significant process differences in the building materials industry, standards or regulations for intelligent factory design, process simulation, quality control, and storage management are formulated around areas such as cement, glass, ceramics, glass fiber, concrete, bricks, wall materials, and mining. Guidelines and standards are also established for 5G-based equipment inspection, defect detection based on artificial intelligence, supply chain collaboration based on industrial cloud, and remote equipment operation and maintenance.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, building materials.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the high safety risks, high control requirements, high energy consumption, and high environmental protection requirements in the petrochemical industry, we will develop factory design specifications such as the intelligent factory information model. We will also establish new technology application standards or regulations for process warning, on-site personnel positioning, equipment health, and operation alarms. Additionally, we will develop application guidelines for remote equipment maintenance.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, petrochemicals.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the overall characteristics of the textile industry, which is characterized by a dispersed and localized manufacturing process, standards or guidelines are developed for the interconnection, information modeling, and remote operation and maintenance technology requirements of specialized equipment in areas such as spinning, chemical fiber, weaving, non-woven, printing and dyeing, clothing, and home textiles. Standards or regulations are also developed for data, logistics and warehousing, and system integration in the process of digital workshop or smart factory construction. Standards or guidelines are established for the application of new models such as mass customization.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, textiles.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the characteristics of the continuous production process, complex technological system, and diversified intermediate states of the steel production process manufacturing industry, standards and specifications have been developed for the application of intelligent technologies in production scenarios, such as 5G applications, unmanned vehicles, and special robots. Standards and specifications have also been developed for intelligent factory construction, including factory design and digital delivery, digital twin models, and standards for intelligent production management, such as quality, logistics, energy, environmental protection, equipment, and supply chain optimization.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, steel

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the characteristics of the rail transit equipment industry, such as multiple varieties, small batch production, emphasis on both new construction and maintenance, and personalized customization, intelligent factory construction is focused on typical business scenarios such as welding, polishing, assembly and debugging, and logistics. Key technical standards are formulated for intelligent equipment testing and certification, three-dimensional model application specifications, industrial robot interfaces, and process technology requirements. Implementation guidelines for intelligent manufacturing projects and application standards for high-speed train remote maintenance are also established.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, rail transit.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the characteristics of the aerospace industry, such as multiple varieties, small batch production, model-based development mode, and multi-party collaboration in design and manufacturing, we will focus on the construction or upgrading of intelligent factories and digital workshops. We will develop standards for model-based digital design, cloud-based collaborative design platforms, virtual simulation of production lines suitable for complex processes, and environmental monitoring. We will also develop standards for the application of industrial big data in predicting and optimizing the production process.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, aerospace.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: Based on the characteristics of the automobile industry, such as strong technological intensity, numerous components, long industrial chains, and a wide variety of segmented vehicle types, as well as complex production processes, standards and guidelines are developed. These standards and guidelines focus on the application of intelligent empowerment technology in processes such as new energy vehicles, traditional fuel vehicle painting, welding, and final assembly. They also include the development of car products based on digital twins, research and design, testing and validation, production line manufacturing, and integration. Additionally, standards and guidelines are established for the development, production, marketing, and supply chain management of large-scale personalized customization in the automotive industry.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, automobile.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT-Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the characteristics of high safety requirements, large differences in raw material quality, complex processes, multiple varieties and small batch production, and frequent logistics scheduling in the non-ferrous metal industry, standards and specifications are formulated for specialized intelligent equipment, smelting and processing processes, including information coding, information exchange, and operation status management. Application guidelines and standards are also established for the design, construction, and production process monitoring of smart factories.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, non-ferrous metals.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT-Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the high technological complexity, fast product iteration, obvious characteristics of small batch production with multiple varieties, and the rapid growth of personalized and customized demands in the electronic information manufacturing industry, standards and specifications are formulated for the production and processing of electronic information materials, components, information communication products, and systems. These standards and specifications include information models and requirements for dedicated intelligent equipment and systems, as well as guidelines for the construction of flexible production lines, digital workshops, and smart factories. Additionally, standards for the application of new models such as personalized customization are also established.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, electronic information.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: In response to the significant characteristics of the power equipment industry, such as a wide range of product types, customization, and high maintenance requirements, guidelines and standards for smart factory construction and system integration have been developed, focusing on areas such as smart grid user terminals and electric motors. Guidelines and standards have also been established for digital simulation of manufacturing processes (including processing, production planning and layout, and logistics simulation), digital processing of resources, digital process control, digital collaborative manufacturing, remote equipment maintenance, customization, and smart manufacturing capability assessment.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, power equipment.

name: Guidelines for the Construction of National Intelligent Manufacturing Standard System (2021 Edition) (MIIT Lianke [2021] No. 187) (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, National Standardization Administration/November 17, 2021)
content: The light industry focuses on areas such as leather, primary batteries, and detergent products, and develops standards for specialized process equipment interconnection, online testing, etc. It also develops guidelines for large-scale personalized customization in areas such as household appliances and furniture. The food industry focuses on areas such as dairy beverages, brewing, frozen food, and preserved food, and develops standards for smart factory design, brewing and filling, process decision-making, remote operation and maintenance, and identification resolution. The agricultural machinery and engineering machinery industry focuses on developing standards for large-scale personalized design, intelligent operation and maintenance monitoring, etc. The printing industry focuses on developing standards for flexible printing process design, intercommunication between systems, etc. The nuclear energy industry focuses on developing standards for data-driven intelligent production. The civil explosive industry focuses on developing standards for key process equipment status monitoring, maintenance requirements, etc.
titlelist: Construction content, industry application standards, others.

name: Notice on Carrying out the Pilot Demonstration Action of Intelligent Manufacturing in 2021 (MIIT Letter No. 263 [2021]) (Issued by the Office of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Office of the National Development and Reform Commission, the Office of the Ministry of Finance, and the Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation on November 2, 2021)
content: Adhering to the principles of basing on national conditions, promoting systematically, selecting and adjusting dynamically, advancing scenario innovation, factory demonstration, and regional pilot, selecting and promoting excellent intelligent scenarios, promoting the construction of demonstration factories for intelligent manufacturing in specific industries through the ranking and leadership approach, encouraging regions with conditions to establish pilot zones for intelligent manufacturing, constructing a pilot demonstration system combining points, lines, and areas, leveraging the driving role of advanced models, accelerating the promotion and application of new technologies, new equipment, and new models. By 2025, a number of intelligent manufacturing demonstration factories with high technological levels and significant demonstration effects will be built, several pilot zones for intelligent manufacturing will be cultivated, a number of intelligent manufacturing excellent scenarios with high technological levels and application value will be refined and summarized, breakthroughs in key technologies, equipment, software, standards, and solutions will be achieved, the pilot application of intelligent manufacturing standards will be promoted, and industry-specific intelligent transformation and upgrading paths will be explored to carry out large-scale promotion and application.
